svg.title: Annex A11 · Disaster memory: historical catalogue, indicators and tab
svg.desc: Past-disaster sources, resumable harvest in GitHub Actions, reading, classification, placement and linking of records, per-area indicators, published files and the tab.
svg.text: Annex A11 · Disaster memory: historical catalogue, indicators and tab

A harvest every 6 hours fetches what is missing from 66 past-disaster sources, builds a catalogue by district with the prevention team's dashboard columns, joins the sources that tell the same event, computes each area's
indicators and opens a PR. Once merged, the Disaster memory tab publishes it.
Details these boxes of the full diagram: Past-disaster archives (66 sources), Historical catalogue harvest (memoria-cosecha.yml), Historical catalogue and indicators (build_historico).

g.title: 1. Event sources → memoria-cosecha.yml: API, ArcGIS and PDF. Long downloads (SINPAD month by month, COEN PDFs, El Peruano, INGEMMET) are saved in parts.
2. Press and old newspapers → memoria-cosecha.yml: searches by term. Only metadata, an excerpt of up to 200 characters and the link: the media's text is not redistributed.
3. Prevention and identified hazard → memoria-cosecha.yml: decrees, reports and layers. Evidence of what was known before each emergency: they are not events.
4. memoria-cosecha.yml → Actions cache: parts and state. Saved at the end of every run, finished or not.
5. Actions cache → memoria-cosecha.yml: resumes. The next run reads the parts and requests only what is missing.

6. memoria-cosecha.yml → Reading and classification: when nothing is missing. build_historico --sin-red --parcial --indices-al-dia: everything comes from the cache, its SHA-256 checked against the manifest, except the ICEN and the ONI, fetched up to date.
7. Curated records → Reading and classification: YAML in the repository. Curated records and reviews live in the repository and are read on every build.
8. Reading and classification → Placement: records. A record without a recognisable place is left out.
9. Placement → Source linking: placed records. Candidates that join no existing event enter as records of their own, if they have a place and a date.
10. Source linking → Quality rules: catalogue. How many rows each rule touched is kept in «calidad» of fuentes.json and resumen.json.
11. Quality rules → Per-area indicators: clean catalogue. Frequency uses only the period's homogeneous source (DesInventar); the others add records and impacts.
12. Per-area indicators → Catalogue PR: new files. The PR shows what changed per source; a person reviews and merges it.
13. Catalogue PR → Published files: on merge to main. The main deploy publishes public/assets/historico/ (annex A8).
14. Published files → Disaster memory tab: reads and recomputes. The tab loads the summary and, when a department is opened, its detail.
15. Published files → Prevention team and public: eventos.csv and CSVs. UTF-8 with BOM so Excel reads accents; an empty impact means «not reported», not zero.
16. Disaster memory tab → Prevention team and public: consults. Each figure with its source, its interval and what it does not say.
Event sources. DesInventar (1970-2015), SINPAD (2015-2026), COEN reports, IDMC, NASA's landslide catalogue and glacial lake outburst floods.

a.title: Annex A1: Sources, reachability and registry

g.title: Press and old newspapers. 44 online media (the public WordPress API, RPP's archive and sitemaps) and Chronicling America (US newspapers from 1836 to 1963 that reprinted cables from Peru).
g.text: RPP's archive and sitemaps) and Chronicling

g.title: Prevention and identified hazard. Emergency declarations from El Peruano, INGEMMET and IGP assessments and inventories, ANA critical points, health facilities hit in 2023 and Red Cross appeals.
g.text: facilities hit in 2023 and Red Cross appeals.

g.title: Curated records. Events from historical studies (García-Herrera et al. since 1550, Eguiguren 1728-1891, the 2017 PIRCC), each with its citation, and the hand corrections in revisiones.yaml.
g.text: 2017 PIRCC), each with its citation, and the

g.title: memoria-cosecha.yml. Every 6 hours: one process per source, in parallel by server and one after another within each, with a 300-minute limit and at least 5 s between requests to the same server. Technology: cosecha_historico.py, build_historico.py.

g.title: Actions cache. The parts of each long download and the harvest state (progress, consecutive failures, last error): the next run continues where it stopped.
g.text: The parts of each long download and the
last error): the next run continues where it

g.title: Catalogue PR. When nothing is missing: the catalogue is built offline and a PR is opened from bot/memoria-desastres/<start> with what changed in each source; ci.yml runs its tests.
g.text: When nothing is missing: the catalogue is
built offline and a PR is opened from
changed in each source; ci.yml runs its tests.

g.title: Reading and classification. Each reader maps its source to the same schema: hazard type from the team's vocabulary (with its IRDR code), date and its precision, impacts and ENSO event from the ICEN. Technology: fuentes.py, desinventar.py, cosecha.py, esquema.py.

schema: hazard type from the team's
vocabulary (with its IRDR code), date and its
precision, impacts and ENSO event from the

g.title: Placement. Current INEI UBIGEO by code or by name; if the name is not enough, the source's point within IGN's boundaries; in free text, the news place finder. Technology: territorio.py, geo.py.
g.text: Current INEI UBIGEO by code or by name; if
the name is not enough, the source's point
within IGN's boundaries; in free text, the news

g.title: Source linking. COEN reports, glacial lakes, news and old newspaper pages are joined to the event they tell (place, compatible hazard and date); the event keeps how many sources corroborate it and their links. Technology: enlace.py.
g.text: COEN reports, glacial lakes, news and old
newspaper pages are joined to the event they
tell (place, compatible hazard and date); the
event keeps how many sources corroborate it

g.title: Quality rules. They join each IDMC row to its SINPAD emergency, fix dates (Lima time, DesInventar's 1 January), lower the confidence of report or publication dates, mark «ICEN pending» and drop news items that are not an event. Also when rebuilding from the catalogue. Technology: build_historico.tidy.
g.text: They join each IDMC row to its SINPAD
confidence of report or publication dates,
mark «ICEN pending» and drop news items
that are not an event. Also when rebuilding

g.title: Per-area indicators. Years with damage (Wilson interval), return period and 5-year probability with their intervals, El Niño ratio (quasi-Poisson), great Niños and «was it known before?» compared with chance, by district, province, department and macro-region, with their out-of-sample validation (2016-2025); the browser recomputes with the same methods. Technology: indicadores.py, historico-model.js, validacion.py.
g.text: Niños and «was it known before?» compared
with chance, by district, province, department

g.title: Published files. eventos.zip (the 13 dashboard columns and 50 metadata columns), the indicators, the per-district context, the prevention files and the data dictionary and browser versions (with finos.json and historia.json, and the named rivers and CENEPRED blocks from tools.build_capas_mapa, for the detail views).
g.text: per-district context, the prevention files and
the data dictionary and browser versions
named rivers and CENEPRED blocks from

g.title: Disaster memory tab. How to use it, map and profile of each area with intervals and, above the map, its detail views (watersheds, rivers and places, damage and poverty with CENEPRED's at-risk blocks), timeline, the great Niños side by side, ranking, the validation, «was it known before?», before 1970, the evidence on prevention and the method with its limits. Technology: historico.js, historico-model.js, historico-evidencia.js, historico-detalle.js.

and poverty with CENEPRED's at-risk blocks),

If something fails: what happens and which fallback takes over
A server does not answer or cuts the download
The download resumes where it stopped in the next run; the harvest table
shows the progress and the last error.
A source the catalogue needs fails again and again
It is never given up: the PR does not open without it and the harvest table
A second-round source (press, evidence) fails three runs in a
It stops being waited for and the catalogue is built without it (--parcial); the
It is accepted, its SHA-256 is updated in the manifest and the PR shows
A site asks for a bot check or a login, or rejects AI use
It is noted and not bypassed; the source is documented as unusable, with
